title: The Theotokos
definition: The Virgin Mary is rightly called Theotokos, 'the one who gave birth to God,' because the child she bore is not a mere man joined to God but the eternal Son of God himself, made man in her womb. The title does not exalt her above her Son; it confesses who her Son is. To deny her this name is to divide the one Christ into two.
tradition: The title Theotokos became the test of orthodoxy at the Third Ecumenical Council in Ephesus (431), against Nestorius, who preferred to call Mary 'Christ-bearer' and so split Christ into two persons. St. Cyril of Alexandria led the Church's confession that the one born of Mary is one and the same Son, God and man.

citations.gloss: Book II, on the title Theotokos: why the Virgin truly gave birth to God.
Her own words: 'all generations shall call me blessed.'
On the name Emmanuel, 'God with us': the child of the Virgin is God in our midst.
On the twofold nativity: born of the Father before the ages, born of the Virgin in time.
The Second Letter to Nestorius: the one Christ may not be divided into two sons.
The Twelfth Anathema, against any who refuse to confess the Word suffered in the flesh.
Against the division of Christ into two sons, the root error of Nestorianism.
